Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-11-01", "authors": [{"authorId": "2509659705", "name": "Kang-Ye Wang"}, {"authorId": "35495931", "name": "Peng-Wen Dai"}, {"authorId": "2259851578", "name": "Chuan Wang"}, {"authorId": "2149215539", "name": "Xiao-Chun Cao"}], "abstract": "Knowledge graph completion (KGC) aims to predict missing relationships between pairs of entities. Recently, Message Passing Neural Networks (MPNNs) have been employed in KGC and demonstrated superior ability in embedding learning. Current methods, however, face two major dilemmas. One focuses on learning complex entity embedding while neglecting the importance of relation embedding learning. The other is that some KGC methods conduct relation embedding learning through a neural network. However, this learning procedure limits learning independence from neighboring entities. To address this issue, we propose a Relation Entity Graph Message Passing mechanism (REGMP) to model the learning of entity-dependent relation embedding. Firstly, REGMP constructs a novel relation entity graph, which transforms relation edges into nodes with new edges and directions. The re-constructed relation entity graph builds a direct linkage between entities and relations during embedding learning. Besides, to conduct the embedding learning on the relation entity graph, we propose a Relation Entity Graph Message-passing mechanism to exploit local and fine-grained information. Moreover, to ease the inevitable over-smoothing problem, we develop a reaction-diffusion message-passing network. Experimental results on three knowledge graph completion datasets, including WN18RR, FB15k-237, and Kinship demonstrate the superiority of REGMP."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "002290091c076eb345cce35f8b6f6d8e23df8f18", "externalIds": {"ArXiv": "2610.23766", "CorpusId": 293546338}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/002290091c076eb345cce35f8b6f6d8e23df8f18", "title": "Logic-Guided Graph Denoising Diffusion Models", "venue": "", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": null, "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23766, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-10-16", "authors": [{"authorId": "2316862023", "name": "Samuel Cognolato"}, {"authorId": "2286767454", "name": "Luciano Serafini"}, {"authorId": "2355706361", "name": "Alessandro Sperduti"}, {"authorId": "2386524087", "name": "Andrea Cavallaro"}], "abstract": "Graph diffusion models are competitive approaches for generating complex graph-structured data. However, when such distributions have strict structural constraints, diffusion models may fail to capture them exactly, resulting in the generation of invalid graphs. In this paper, we propose a method for grounding graph diffusion models in domain-specific knowledge via First Order Logic (FOL), leveraging its expressive and interpretable formalism to impose structural constraints on the generative process. We incorporate domain knowledge using classifier guidance, a technique that conditions the diffusion model's distribution on external variables to exert control over the sampled data. During the generative process, classifier guidance steers the denoising trajectory to optimize an objective function, which we define as a fuzzy and differentiable relaxation of the logical rules. Our methodology requires only the specification of constraints in FOL, whose satisfaction is encouraged at inference time to guide a pre-trained generative model. We evaluate our approach by comparing the unconditional generation of knowledge graphs with our logic-guided framework, which incorporates domain ontologies as structural constraints during inference. This approach significantly increases the proportion of generated graphs that satisfy the ontological constraints."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "19a036221cd93923a8799b8e04e115baf3980267", "externalIds": {"ArXiv": "2610.18198", "CorpusId": 292895775}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/19a036221cd93923a8799b8e04e115baf3980267", "title": "QORH: Learning Query-Specific Ordered Rule Hypergraphs for Inductive Knowledge Graph Link Prediction", "venue": "", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": null, "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18198, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-10-13", "authors": [{"authorId": "2333521206", "name": "Nai-Xing Xu"}], "abstract": "Knowledge graph link prediction involving unseen entities and relations requires learning transferable reasoning patterns from observed graph structure. Existing methods based on relation graphs primarily capture pairwise dependencies, limiting their ability to preserve the compositional semantics, relation ordering, and role information of complete path rules. To address this limitation, we propose QORH (Query-specific Ordered Rule Hypergraph), which jointly encodes rule heads and ordered rule bodies as hyperedges conditioned on the query relation, explicitly modeling joint dependencies among multiple relations. QORH performs learnable rule selection using statistical evidence, such as rule confidence and coverage, and enhances relation representations through role-aware hypergraph message passing to guide entity-level reasoning. The model's shared parameters are independent of specific entity or relation identifiers, enabling inductive prediction for unseen entities and relations. Extensive experiments on entity-inductive and fully inductive benchmarks demonstrate that QORH significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art baselines included in our evaluation, validating the effectiveness of rule hypergraph modeling for inductive link prediction."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "c49bcb2c64007447bef86e9e8751d5be4b6347a5", "externalIds": {"DOI": "10.1007/s41060-026-01315-2", "CorpusId": 292803605}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/c49bcb2c64007447bef86e9e8751d5be4b6347a5", "title": "Robust multimodal knowledge graph completion under missing text modality", "venue": "International Journal of Data Science and Analysis", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": "CLOSED", "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: The following paper fields have been elided by the publisher: {'abstract'}. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-10-11", "authors": [{"authorId": "2205543105", "name": "Cosimo Gregucci"}, {"authorId": "2188243473", "name": "Daniel Hern\u00e1ndez"}, {"authorId": "14341992", "name": "Antonio Vergari"}, {"authorId": "2313916215", "name": "Steffen Staab"}], "abstract": "Knowledge graph (KG) foundation models (KGFMs) predict links on unseen graphs zero-shot. KGFMs have been pioneered by ULTRA which builds a relation graph from co-occurrences that match motif templates, and passes messages over it to obtain relation representations. More recent KGFMs such as MOTIF and TRIX increase the size of this relation graph, and FLOCK replaces message-passing with probabilistic random-walk ensembles. However, larger relation graphs mean more messages, and more walks mean more sequences to encode, so they improve performance at higher training and inference cost. This cost hinders their use in more complex reasoning tasks, such as complex query answering. To reverse this trend, we design MERIT, the first KGFM with a transformer relation encoder: every relation name attends to every other, and the motifs enter as a soft prior rather than as edges. Over 56 benchmarks, MERIT matches the zero-shot MRR of SoTA KGFMs while being 6x faster than TRIX and over 100x faster than FLOCK at inference. Fine-tuned for complex query answering like UltraQuery, MERITQuery improves over it at matched cost."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "73c13a9cf80c67dc4a75a1bbef1ba72a91e75e2d", "externalIds": {"ArXiv": "2610.13722", "CorpusId": 292830856}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/73c13a9cf80c67dc4a75a1bbef1ba72a91e75e2d", "title": "Enhancing Legal Reasoning in Pre-trained Language Models via Knowledge Graph-Guided Multi-Task Pre-training", "venue": "", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": null, "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13722, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-10-09", "authors": [{"authorId": "2507639104", "name": "Ibrahim Siddig"}, {"authorId": "34684347", "name": "Munir Georges"}], "abstract": "Legal language understanding requires reasoning over semi-structured regulatory documents, yet standard pre-training objectives do not explicitly target this structural capability. Because current legal language models rely solely on masked language modeling, they treat statutory text as flat token sequences and ignore the underlying hierarchical constraints. To bridge this gap, we present a multi-task pre-training approach for German traffic law (StVO). Our approach combines three complementary objectives: Next Sentence Prediction (NSP), Knowledge Graph (KG) Guided Clustering (CLU), and Knowledge Graph (KG) Aware Paragraph Classification (CLS). This approach explicitly encodes structured legal knowledge directly into the model weights. This encoding enables zero-shot legal reasoning at inference time and removes the need for discrete graph traversal. We evaluate our approach across nine Transformer-based encoders and 324 experimental runs. On synthetic StVO question answering, our models demonstrate consistent relative improvements between 10.3% and 155.0% over baselines. Furthermore, relative to the established LexGLUE baselines (Chalkidis et al., 2022), our models improve over prior results on four of seven legal benchmarks. It also achieves consistent zero-shot transfer gains between 3.4% and 15.8% on Austrian driving regulations. These experimental results indicate that our training approach generalizes successfully beyond the initial training legal domain."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "32139cc488c9b3e7c007ffc3711029483f883fdd", "externalIds": {"DOI": "10.1145/3815178", "CorpusId": 292699943}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/32139cc488c9b3e7c007ffc3711029483f883fdd", "title": "A Sequential Condition Evolution and Interaction Knowledge Graph Framework for Traditional Chinese Medicine Recommendation", "venue": "ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": "CLOSED", "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1145/3815178?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.1145/3815178, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Pan"}, {"authorId": "2244772324", "name": "Zheng-An Yao"}], "abstract": "The ancient art of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) is distinguished by its extensive annals of utilizing nature's botanical emissaries to ameliorate various pathological conditions. TCM diagnosis and treatment exhibit a pronounced degree of personalization and an organically holistic approach, necessitating a comprehensive consideration of the patient's evolving physiological and symptomatic states over temporal domains. However, existing methods for TCM recommendation represent a flaw in accounting for the dynamic oscillations in patients\u2019 conditions, instead restricting their explorations to potential correlative patterns between symptomatic presentations and prescribed remedies. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for optimizing TCM recommendations based on Sequential Condition Evolution and Interaction Knowledge Graphs SCEIKG, an innovation framework that conceptualizes the method as a sequential prescription-making problem by considering the inherent dynamism of patients\u2019 conditions across multiple diagnoses. Furthermore, we incorporate an interaction knowledge graph to enhance the accuracy of recommendations by considering the intricate interplay between various herbs and patients\u2019 states. Experimental results on the real-world dataset demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing TCM recommendation methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance. The source code of SCEIKG is available at https://github.com/jzephyrl/SCEIKG-TCM."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "301cb000b76c864136205adfc52855e07ce46feb", "externalIds": {"ArXiv": "2610.09927", "CorpusId": 292700828}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/301cb000b76c864136205adfc52855e07ce46feb", "title": "KGATE : a Knowledge Graph Embedding Training Environment", "venue": "", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": null, "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09927, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Bri\u00e8re"}, {"authorId": "2508675641", "name": "C\u00e9lia Brahimi"}, {"authorId": "2508676098", "name": "Antoine Toffano"}, {"authorId": "50023381", "name": "Ana\u00efs Baudot"}], "abstract": "Knowledge graph embedding (KGE) models encode the entities and relations of a knowledge graph into a low-dimensional latent space, enabling tasks such as classification or link prediction. Most KGE models follow an autoencoder architecture, in which an encoder projects the knowledge graph into the latent space and a decoder reconstruct it. Combining both encoder and decoder components is increasingly needed, yet existing libraries rarely support complete autoencoders, are often unmaintained, rely on undocumented default hyperparameters, and produce results that cannot be compared across libraries. Here we present KGATE (Knowledge Graph Autoencoder Training Environment), a modular Python library built on PyTorch Geometric and TorchKGE. KGATE lets users assemble initializers, encoders, decoders, losses, negative samplers, and evaluation metrics as building blocks, or plug in their own block. KGATE includes a preprocessing procedure that controls data leakage, a builtin training pipeline, and reproducibility by design. Benchmarks against six existing KGE libraries show that KGATE training time is comparable with the fastest libraries while offering a broader set of features."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "ea53fca071c331f99aad9c37660e443cd181130c", "externalIds": {"DBLP": "journals/kbs/NingDTCXT26", "DOI": "10.1016/j.knosys.2026.116631", "CorpusId": 290093898}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/ea53fca071c331f99aad9c37660e443cd181130c", "title": "Synergistic relation learning via difficulty-aware curriculum and conditional diffusion for few-shot knowledge graph completion", "venue": "Knowledge-Based Systems", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": "CLOSED", "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1016/j.knosys.2026.116631?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.1016/j.knosys.2026.116631, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content.
